title: The Salafi approach
hook: a movement to follow the early generations closely and avoid later additions, itself diverse

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Tablighi Jamaat, and your line: preaching by traveling. Small groups knocking on doors, mostly to remind other Muslims to come to prayer. Did you pass one good thing on in person, not by text? Day one thousand three hundred seventy-two.

A chain of people, hand to hand. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says something. A companion hears it and passes it on. Someone who learned from that companion passes it on again. Al-Bukhari keeps a saying about those first links. In paraphrase: the best people are my generation, then those who come after them, then those who come after them. Some Muslims hear that saying and draw a plain conclusion. If the first links in the chain were the best, then the surest way to practice Islam is to stand as close to them as you can. That is the starting point of today's movement, told in its own words.
screen: `A CHAIN, HAND TO HAND.` → `MY GENERATION, THEN THE NEXT.` → `STAND CLOSE TO THE FIRST.`

segments.voice: First, the name, as Salafis explain it. They take it from a phrase, al-salaf al-salih, which they render as the righteous predecessors: the companions and the generations who learned from them. A Salafi, in their own description, is someone who follows the Qur'an and the Sunnah as those early generations understood them. Second, what they avoid. Salafi teachers point to a hadith in al-Bukhari and Muslim. In paraphrase: whoever brings into this matter of ours something that is not part of it, it is rejected. So they are wary of practices they see as later additions, and they ask of any devotion: did the Prophet and his companions do this? Belief in Allah's oneness, tawhid, sits at the center of how they teach. Third, the movement is itself diverse. There is no single Salafi headquarters. Some teachers focus on study and personal practice and stay out of public life. Others take part in it. Salafis argue with each other about method, about politics, about how strict to be with a person who disagrees. Lumping them together misses the arguments they have among themselves. Fourth, the conversation around them. Muslims who are not Salafi also love the first generations, and say so. Scholars of the traditional schools hold that the schools, and the long line of later scholarship, are how a Muslim reaches those generations faithfully, not a step away from them. Salafis answer that the texts should be read directly, with the early generations as the guide. Each side says it is following the companions. They differ about the road back.
screen: `AL-SALAF AL-SALIH: THE PREDECESSORS.` · `IS IT SOMETHING NEW? THEN IT'S REJECTED.` · `ITSELF DIVERSE, AND ARGUING.` · `EACH SIDE SAYS: THE COMPANIONS.`

segments.voice: The practice is to let a movement describe itself before anyone else describes it. Settle, and breathe. Bring back the chain from the hook: a saying passed from hand to hand. Let each breath be one link. The Prophet. A companion. The one who learned from that companion. Stay with the chain for a few breaths, without judging anyone in it. Later today, if you're curious, read one short page by a Salafi teacher explaining the approach in their own words, and notice what they say they are doing. If you pray, you can make your own prayer in your own words. The bell holds the time.
The Salafi approach. A movement that aims to follow the Qur'an and the Sunnah as the first generations understood them, wary of later additions, and diverse inside itself. Today's word.

Your line: back to the first generations. This week took us through days for everyone, many ways of being Muslim, the mosque, the imam, Deobandi and Barelvi, the Tablighi Jamaat, and now the Salafis. Today, notice one habit you keep and ask where it came from. Tomorrow, traditional Sufi orders today. Day one thousand three hundred seventy-two.

howItsDone: Salafi Muslims describe their approach as following the Qur'an and the Sunnah as the companions and the generations after them understood them, studying the texts directly and avoiding devotions they regard as later additions; they differ among themselves on method and on public life.

match.prompt: the Salafi approach — tap the pairs.

myth: Salafis all agree with each other on method and politics
they argue among themselves; some stay out of public life, others take part.

they explain it from al-salaf al-salih, the righteous predecessors.

fork.setup: you're a Salafi teacher and someone asks about a devotion you've never heard of. what's the first question you ask?
options: is it popular where you live?
did the Prophet and his companions do this?
does it feel meaningful to you?
fork.reveal: in their own description, Salafis measure a practice by whether the first generations did it, pointing to the hadith that something new brought into the religion is rejected.

original.note: Arabic: one who follows the salaf, the predecessors, as Salafis explain their own name.

trapdoor: what you thought: Salafis are one single group that all thinks alike.
what it means: a movement that aims to follow the Qur'an and Sunnah as the first generations understood them, and that argues inside itself about method and public life.
what a scholar hears: the hadith of the best generations, the hadith on rejected additions, and the old conversation with the traditional schools about how best to reach the companions.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2652 (the best people are my generation, then those after them, then those after them)
